references.text: David speaks of healing and salvation as gifts from God, reflecting Jesus' instructions to his disciples to heal the sick without cost.
Isaiah prophesies about one who will come to heal the brokenhearted and set captives free, which resembles Jesus' command to heal and cast out demons for free.
Jesus refers to his own deeds as the fulfillment of Isaiah's prophecy, including healing and raising the dead, which he also instructs his disciples to do.
Peter heals a lame man in Jesus' name, demonstrating the same power and authority that Jesus gave to his disciples.
Paul raises Eutychus from the dead, showing that the apostles' actions continued in line with Jesus' instructions.
